title: The Impossible Product Manager: why a great PM team beats a mythical great PM
summary: Jason Cohen argues that "Great PM" checklists describe an impossible superhuman. He splits product management into four roles (Strategist, Customer Whisperer, Scrum Product Owner, Orchestrator) and says one person can be excellent at one, good at a second, and no more. The leader's job is designing a team that covers all four.

principles.text: A great PM is excellent at one area, good at another, and has no time for a third.
principles.quote: A "Great PM" is excellent in one area, good in at least one other, and doesn't have time for more than two.

principles.text: Don't hunt unicorns. Assemble excellence across the whole product team in all four areas.
principles.quote: While one person cannot be all things to all people, across the entire product team, you do need excellence in all four areas.

principles.text: Product management centers on deciding what to build, fed by strategy and customer research, then execution and coordination.
principles.quote: The role and scope of "Product Manager" varies between companies, but the role centers on deciding what to build

principles.text: Strategy means saying no to most ideas so you can say yes to exactly the right ones.
principles.quote: Having the fortitude to make decisions that will affect us for years, and cause us to say "no" to 90% of our ideas, so we say "yes" to exactly the right ideas.

principles.text: Revenue and retention are outputs of strategy plus execution, not a strategy or operational goal themselves.
principles.quote: revenue and retention are outputs of great strategy plus great execution, not themselves a strategy or even an operational goal.

principles.text: Even small improvements in team design matter, because most organizations have excellence nowhere in these roles.
principles.quote: Even incremental improvements here can be impactful, because so often organizations have excellence nowhere.
